summary: Clean on the design/simplification dimension. signatures.py is a flat data table built by merging three logically-grouped sub-dicts (signatures_c/_m/_sqlite) with a single named type alias (lldiv_t). No duplication, no over-complexity, no dead entries, consistent typing, and signatures accurate to the C headers. Every defined entry is reachable (either through a _*.py wrapper or directly via _call_lib_func name lookup) and every wrapper/_call_lib_func-requested name is defined; no orphans either way. The platform-variable-type hazard (long/time_t/size_t) is deliberately avoided by omitting the affected functions, matching the documented policy. No findings.
